standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice sorting clothing. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: Before any washing instruction, the learner is given (or gathers) a mixed pile of at least eight clothing items and sorts them using their own best guess at the rule that matters for washing, then compares that sort to what a care label suggests.
safetyNotes: Handling clean, dry clothing only; no washer or dryer operation in this lesson.

simulationAlternative.description: If eight real clothing items aren't available to sort, the learner instead sorts eight items from a printed or hand-drawn clothing set using the same one-rule method and checks their rule against a sample care label provided in the lesson.

materials: learner-local: at least eight clothing items

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u02-l01-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u02-l01-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u02-l01-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u02-l01-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Check one item's care label. Does your sorting rule match what the label says that item needs? If not, what would you change about your rule?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u02-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g5-u02-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g5-u02-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Consistent sorting rule: One rule applied consistently across all items. | Label comparison: Checks the label and accurately states whether it matches their rule. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u02-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Sort the same pile a second way, using a different rule than the first time (for example fabric type instead of color), and compare which rule would actually matter more on wash day.

duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: sorting clothing worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Before any washing instruction, the learner is given (or gathers) a mixed pile of at least eight clothing items and sorts them using their own best guess at the rule that matters for washing, then compares that sort to what a care label suggests.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact sorting clothing decision or action.
Model move 2: Before sorting, predict: what do you think matters most when sorting clothes for washing — color, fabric, or something else?
Model move 3: Sort your pile of at least eight items into at least three groups using one consistent rule, then write down the rule you used.
Model check: Consistent sorting rule: One rule applied consistently across all items. | Label comparison: Checks the label and accurately states whether it matches their rule.

resources.title: sorting clothing action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for sorting clothing.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u02-l01-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g5-u02-l01-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g5-u02-l01-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g5-u02-l01-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g5-u02-l01-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: sorting clothing coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Before any washing instruction, the learner is given (or gathers) a mixed pile of at least eight clothing items and sorts them using their own best guess at the rule that matters for washing, then compares that sort to what a care label suggests.
Coach direction: Before sorting, predict: what do you think matters most when sorting clothes for washing — color, fabric, or something else?
Learner prompt: State your prediction and reasoning.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: sorting clothing complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Sort your pile of at least eight items into at least three groups using one consistent rule, then write down the rule you used.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I used the same rule for every item, not a different reason for each pile.
Response 2 (t2-p2): State the sorting rule you used in one sentence.

Equal-access rule: If eight real clothing items aren't available to sort, the learner instead sorts eight items from a printed or hand-drawn clothing set using the same one-rule method and checks their rule against a sample care label provided in the lesson.

resources.title: sorting clothing minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Check one item's care label. Does your sorting rule match what the label says that item needs? If not, what would you change about your rule?
Success checks: Consistent sorting rule: One rule applied consistently across all items. | Label comparison: Checks the label and accurately states whether it matches their rule.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: sorting clothing supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g5-u02-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g5-u02-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional sorting clothing condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Consistent sorting rule: One rule applied consistently across all items. | Label comparison: Checks the label and accurately states whether it matches their rule..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u02-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.
